description:
Blocking prerequisite for PETIR (op-chyp). Determine which of outram-foam-basic-lib's general-numerics modules can move to a standalone crate WITHOUT dragging the FV layer with them.

Audit, per module: does it reference fields / fv_operators / mesh / ldu_matrix / limiters, directly or transitively?

  math (11,188 lines)        differentiate, minimise, erf_inv, inc_gamma, inv_inc_gamma
  ode (6,167)                suspected entangled — check first
  krylov (3,859)
  primitives (3,070)         tensor algebra
  polynomial (1,015)
  linear_operator (904)      already generic by construction (added for farrer-park)
  matrix (420)
  interpolation (275)

Deliverable: a table of movable / entangled / stays-put with the specific
coupling named for each entangled one. Report it; do NOT start moving code.

Line counts measured 2026-09-14; re-measure rather than trusting them.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
AUDIT DELIVERED 2026-09-14. Report only -- NO code moved, as the bean required.

HEADLINE: 'entangled with the FV layer' is almost entirely FALSE. Of 26,881 lines, 23,022 have ZERO code coupling to fields/fv_operators/mesh/ldu_matrix/limiters. Only krylov is entangled.

  module           lines   verdict      coupling
  math            11,171   MOVABLE      0 code refs
  ode              6,167   MOVABLE      0 code refs
  krylov           3,859   ENTANGLED    14 real uses of crate::ldu_matrix{,::parallel}
  primitives       3,070   MOVABLE      0
  polynomial       1,015   MOVABLE      0
  linear_operator    904   MOVABLE      0
  matrix             420   MOVABLE      0
  interpolation      275   MOVABLE      0

THE TRAP I ALMOST FELL INTO: a naive grep for crate::fields / crate::fv_operators / crate::ldu_matrix reports math=3 files, ode=1, krylov=5, linear_operator=1 -- suggesting math and ode are coupled. They are NOT. Every hit in math, ode and linear_operator is a RUSTDOC INTRA-DOC LINK in a /// or //! comment (e.g. [crate::fields::parallel::FIELD_PARALLEL_CROSSOVER] cited when documenting a parallel crossover threshold). Excluding comment lines, math/ode/linear_operator drop to 0. Anyone re-running this must exclude comments or they will conclude the opposite.

KRYLOV's 14 real couplings, all on ldu_matrix only (not fields/mesh/limiters):
  bicgstab.rs:69,70  gmres.rs:88,89  mod.rs:134
  preconditioner.rs:40,41,44,431  hybrid_tests.rs:100,101,872,1585,1853
It needs ldu_matrix's parallel vecops (dot, axpy, vecop_backend_for). Either move ldu_matrix's vector ops with it, or abstract them behind linear_operator (which is already generic by construction, added for farrer-park).

TWO COSTS NOT IN THE BEAN's FRAMING:
1. rayon. math (6 files), ode (2) and krylov use rayon. The epic says PETIR takes NO rayon (rayon-core needs OS threads, builds on neither no_std nor wasm). So math and ode are movable as to the FV layer but NOT as-is into a no_std PETIR -- their parallelism has to be stripped or feature-gated first. That is a bigger job than the separability question.
2. Doc links break on the move. The intra-doc links above become dangling when the module leaves the crate, which is minor but will fail a docs build.

CLEANEST FIRST MOVE: polynomial + linear_operator + matrix + interpolation = 1,710 lines, ZERO FV coupling AND zero rayon/std imports. That set can go to PETIR today with no untangling at all.

title: PETIR: separability audit of outram-foam-basic-lib's general-maths modules

notes.content:

design:
Add `outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs` to the declared-mature / Haiku-dogfooded set.
It is now on the critical path for the nuclear-refinery work and needs the same
public-API gate as the other declared crates.

Programme method and constraints as established in #58 and #63.

## Why it is being promoted

The Python wheel has already been independently dogfooded through the public
bindings, and this workflow ran end to end:

```
BlackOilCrude
    -> pseudo-component characterization
    -> CrudeColumnConfig
    -> Peng-Robinson 1978 thermodynamics
    -> rigorous MESH column
    -> steady-state crude cut slate
```

`BlackOilCrude::heavy()` with `CrudeColumnConfig::atmospheric_default()` and 12
pseudo-components converged in **38 iterations** to a final error of **~8.5e-7**
for a 1 mol/s feed, giving:

| cut | mol/s |
|---|---|
| naphtha | 0.15005 |
| kerosene | 0.04001 |
| diesel | 0.03335 |
| heavier diesel draw | 0.02668 |
| atmospheric residue | 0.74991 |
| **total** | **1.00000** |

**This proves the public execution path exists and is useful. It does not
prove refinery-grade predictive accuracy.** Treat API maturity and
physics-validation evidence as separate things throughout.

## Verified while filing (2026-09-05)

Checked rather than assumed:

- `BlackOilCrude`, `BlackOilCrude::heavy()`, `CrudeColumnConfig`,
  `CrudeColumnConfig::atmospheric_default()` and `solve_crude_column` all exist
  as named.
- `heavy()` is **22.0 degAPI**, so SG = 141.5/(22+131.5) = **0.9218** — matches
  the reported figure exactly.
- Crate state: version 0.0.3, **682 `#[test]` markers**, **no prelude at all**,
  **1 example**.
- **No `VacuumColumn` exists.**

Absent prelude was the single most predictive defect across the seven crates
dogfooded in #58 — the two worst failures there were both prelude failures.

## The four fidelity axes

The maturity documentation must distinguish these, because they carry
genuinely different evidence levels:

1. thermodynamic / property-package maturity
2. rigorous MESH numerical-solver maturity
3. crude pseudo-component characterization maturity
4. **refinery-unit-model fidelity**

Axis 4 is currently the weakest and the crate already says so — see the
sub-issue on the CDU model.

## Deliverables

1. maturity declaration
2. fresh Haiku public-API dogfood
3. saved friction logs
4. genuine API defect fixes
5. public tutorials
6. regression tests for discovered defects
7. independently validated thermodynamics and column numerics
8. documented refinery-model fidelity limitations
9. determination of whether VDU is currently expressible
10. focused issues for missing refinery functionality — **do not
    opportunistically implement the whole refinery**

## Branch

`develop` only. **Do not merge or push to `main` as part of this task.**
title: Declare outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs mature and dogfood it (nuclear-refinery critical path)

description:
Build real CSV file logging into app_scaffold. Confirmed by survey (2026-08-17) that no
real file-writing CSV export exists anywhere in this crate: ciet_educational_simulator_v2's
'csv' pages (heater_page.rs ciet_sim_heater_page_csv, and fhr_sim_v2's equivalent
graph_pages/mod.rs) render a scrollable on-screen ui.label() text dump, not a file.
htgr_sim_v1/fhr_sim_v2 have zero CSV code beyond that fake display. The `csv` crate is
already a workspace dependency (csv = "1.4.0", root Cargo.toml, consumed today only by
tuas_boussinesq_solver via csv.workspace = true) -- reuse it rather than hand-rolling
comma-joining, and add csv.workspace = true to outram-park-digital-twin-engine's own
Cargo.toml.

Design: CsvLogger wrapping csv::Writer<File>, created with a header row, a
maybe_write_row() that no-ops unless a configurable interval has elapsed since the last
write (mirrors the existing graph_data_record_interval_seconds convention from the CIET
v1 lineage, so a future migration of that convention is a drop-in). Additive only in
this pass -- no existing simulator is wired to it yet; that's follow-up work once this
lands and each simulator decides its own column set.

Surveyed 2026-08-17, read-only, by a fork agent; report retained in op-wqk.22.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Implemented: CsvLogger in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/app_scaffold/csv_logging.rs, wraps csv::Writer<File> with interval throttling via a caller-supplied Instant. Added csv.workspace = true to the crate's Cargo.toml (crate already declared as a workspace dep for tuas_boussinesq_solver, no new version). 7 unit tests, all green, including a comma-escaping round-trip test. Re-exported from app_scaffold::{CsvLogger, CsvLoggerError}. Additive only -- no existing simulator wired to it yet.

title: app_scaffold: CsvLogger -- opt-in real CSV file export for real-time simulators

description: Goal: all workspace crates' non-GUI library code builds for Android (aarch64-linux-android + armv7/x86_64 emulator). Mechanism: Android-hostile deps (ndarray-linalg / system BLAS-LAPACK, C/Fortran toolchains, GUI/windowing) are target-gated OFF Android, and any test/bench/example using them is cfg(not(target_os=android))-gated so it does not compile there. Standing rule now in the workspace CLAUDE.md ('Android portability'). GUI (egui/eframe) items are out of scope for Android.
title: Android support: every crate's non-GUI code compiles/runs on Android
